questions.stem: A student says that when you go to the toilet to pass faeces, this is excretion. Why is this statement incorrect?

options.text: Because faeces are formed in the kidneys, not the intestines
Because egestion (removal of undigested food) is not the same as excretion (removal of metabolic waste)
Because faeces contain metabolic waste products from cells
Because excretion only occurs in plants, not animals

questions.explanation: Excretion is specifically the removal of waste products produced by metabolic reactions inside cells (e.g., CO₂ from respiration, urea from amino acid breakdown). Faeces mainly consist of undigested food that never entered cells, so their removal is called egestion, not excretion.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide is described as an excretory product. Which metabolic process produces the CO₂ that the body needs to excrete?

options.text: Digestion of food in the stomach
Aerobic respiration in cells
Absorption of nutrients in the small intestine
Filtration of blood in the kidneys

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a waste product of aerobic respiration (glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water). It is produced in cells and must be excreted via the lungs because a build-up of CO₂ would make the blood too acidic.

questions.stem: A patient with liver disease has elevated levels of ammonia in their blood. Why is this dangerous, and what process is failing?

options.text: The liver is failing to convert ammonia to urea; ammonia is toxic and damages cells
The liver is producing too much bile, which contains ammonia
The kidneys are sending ammonia back to the liver instead of excreting it
Ammonia is building up because the patient is eating too much fat

questions.explanation: When excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver, the amino group is removed and forms ammonia, which is highly toxic. Normally, the liver quickly converts ammonia to the less toxic urea. If the liver is diseased, ammonia accumulates in the blood, which can damage the brain and other organs.

questions.stem: A doctor explains that the kidneys, lungs, and skin are all excretory organs. Which waste product is excreted by both the lungs and the skin?

options.text: Urea
Bile
Water
Glucose

questions.explanation: Water is a metabolic waste product of aerobic respiration. It is excreted by the lungs (in exhaled air as water vapour), the skin (in sweat), and the kidneys (in urine). Urea is excreted only by the kidneys, and glucose is not a waste product.

questions.stem: Why is it essential that metabolic waste products are removed from the body rather than being allowed to accumulate?

options.text: Waste products take up space that is needed for storing nutrients
Waste products are toxic or can disrupt homeostasis, for example by changing blood pH or water balance
Waste products block blood vessels and prevent blood flow
Waste products are converted into harmful vitamins if not removed

questions.explanation: Metabolic waste products like CO₂ and urea can be toxic at high concentrations. CO₂ lowers blood pH (acidosis), and excess urea can damage cells. Excretion maintains the stable internal environment (homeostasis) that cells need to function properly.
